question: Bind — DEF, eco round, 2v2, score 7-7, 1:02 left, no spike. You hold B Site with a Bucky (shotgun), looking up at B Window (Hookah window). Your ult is available. Two attackers are somewhere off-site. What is the highest-EV defensive play?

options.label: Hold tight against cover at B Site watching the Hookah window angle — let the attacker come to you at close range where the Bucky wins
options.explication_courte: The Bucky's edge is close range and pre-aim. Holding the Hookah window angle from B Site means any attacker who drops through is at 5-7m — inside Bucky one-shot territory. You're playing to your weapon's strength and making them come to you.

sources_option.citation: Eco rounds with close-range weapons are won by holding tight angles at the range your weapon dominates — make the enemy walk into your effective range

options.label: Pop your ultimate now to get information on the two attackers and push toward them
options.explication_courte: Spending your ultimate to push into their ground inverts the Bucky's advantage — you're taking long-range duels with a shotgun while they can still be waiting at the angle they chose. The ult is better spent stabilizing the round after you confirm a kill.

sources_option.citation: Agent ultimates on eco rounds are most valuable as stabilizers after a pick, not as initiators that commit you to worse weapon matchups

options.label: Peek out to B Long looking for an early pick before they get set up in their positions
options.explication_courte: Peeking B Long with a Bucky means walking into rifle range (15-25m) where the shotgun does chip damage and the enemy Vandal/Phantom one-taps. You play your worst matchup, wide-open, with no cover, in a round where your only edge is close-angle advantage.

sources_option.citation: Eco players with close-range weapons must not peek long sightlines — take favorable angles and let the enemy commit into shotgun range

options.label: Fall back to CT and set up a passive hold so you can't be smoked out of the B Site angle
options.explication_courte: Retreating to CT gives you a second angle but stretches the B-Long-to-CT rotation too thin in a 2v2 — the remaining defender alone can't hold B site while you're 30m away. Splitting a 2v2 into two 1v1s is a risky call when one player is on a Bucky.

sources_option.citation: In a 2v2 defense, splitting too wide turns the round into isolated 1v1s where the team with better weapons wins each; keep guns mutually supporting

explication_longue: In an eco round 2v2 at 7-7, your Bucky defines what plays are available to you. The shotgun has a decisive close-range advantage — inside 5-7m it can one-tap through armor, but past 12m it does chip damage that loses a gunfight to any rifle. Holding the Hookah window angle from B Site is the play that maximizes that edge: any attacker who drops through the window into B Site lands at close range, right in your kill zone. You are making them come to you at the range you control. Spending your ultimate to push out toward them inverts every advantage — you move into rifle territory with a shotgun, the element of surprise is yours to squander, and you risk an isolated 1v1 under their conditions. Peeking B Long is even worse: 20+ metres of open corridor against rifles is a guaranteed loss. Falling back to CT keeps you alive longer but splits the two defenders so far apart that the attackers can isolate and pick them one at a time. Eco rounds are not lost by bad aim; they're lost by players with close-range weapons taking long-range fights. Hold B site, hold the window, let the Bucky do its job.

sources.citation: Eco rounds are won by playing to your weapon's strength and forcing the enemy into your effective range
